wc.heading: Accounts Receivable Securitization Program
wc.text:
As described in Note 20. “Financial Instruments, Guarantees With Off-Balance-Sheet Risk and Other Guarantees” of the accompanying consolidated financial statements, the Company entered into an accounts receivable securitization program during 2017. The securitization program was amended in February 2023 to increase the available funding capacity from $175.0 million to $225.0 million and adjust the relevant interest rate for borrowings to a SOFR plus an applicable margin. Funding capacity is limited to the availability of eligible receivables and is accounted for as a secured borrowing. Funding capacity under the program may also be utilized for letters of credit in support of other obligations, which has been the Company’s primary utilization. At December 31, 2024, the Company had no outstanding borrowings and $60.4 million of letters of credit outstanding under the program. The Company was not required to post cash collateral under the securitization program at December 31, 2024.

The accounts receivable securitization program was amended in January 2025 to extend its maturity to January 2028.

wc.heading: Accounts Receivable Securitization Program
wc.text:
As described in Note 12. “Financial Instruments and Other Guarantees” of the accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements, the Company entered into an accounts receivable securitization program during 2017. The securitization program provides up to $225.0 million of funding capacity which is accounted for as a secured borrowing, limited to the availability of eligible receivables, and may be secured by a combination of collateral and the trade receivables underlying the program. Funding capacity under the program may also be utilized for letters of credit in support of other obligations, which has been the Company’s primary utilization. At June 30, 2026, the Company had no outstanding borrowings and $62.0 million of letters of credit outstanding under the program. The Company was not required to post cash collateral under the securitization program at June 30, 2026.

The accounts receivable securitization program was amended in January 2025 to extend its maturity to January 2028.

intro.text: Peabody is a leading producer of metallurgical and thermal coal. The Company owned interests in 16 active coal mining operations located in the United States (U.S.) and Australia at December 31, 2025. Included in that count is Peabody’s 50% equity interest in Middlemount Coal Pty Ltd. (Middlemount). During 2025, Peabody continued to advance the development of the Centurion Mine, an underground longwall metallurgical coal mine in Queensland, Australia. Full-scale longwall production commenced in February 2026. The mine is expected to enhance both the quantity and quality of the Company’s production from the Seaborne Metallurgical reportable segment.

wc.heading: Accounts Receivable Securitization Program
wc.text:
As described in Note 20. “Financial Instruments, Guarantees With Off-Balance-Sheet Risk and Other Guarantees” of the accompanying consolidated financial statements, the Company entered into an accounts receivable securitization program during 2017. The securitization program was amended in February 2023 to increase the available funding capacity from $175.0 million to $225.0 million and adjust the relevant interest rate for borrowings to a SOFR plus an applicable margin. Funding capacity is limited to the availability of eligible receivables and is accounted for as a secured borrowing. Funding capacity under the program may also be utilized for letters of credit in support of other obligations, which has been the Company’s primary utilization. At December 31, 2024, the Company had no outstanding borrowings and $60.4 million of letters of credit outstanding under the program. The Company was not required to post cash collateral under the securitization program at December 31, 2024.

The accounts receivable securitization program was amended in January 2025 to extend its maturity to January 2028.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
